test_title: PYST 12: SSC GD Constable 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 07 Feb, 2025 - Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Ketan has two grandsons Mahesh and David. 15 year old Mahesh gets some money from Ketan’s wealth and 16 year old David gets rest of the money. But Mahesh and David will get money only when they turn 22 years old. Till then the money is in a bank getting interest at rate 10% compounded annually. When both turn 22, they receive the same amount. How much had Ketan given David (in ₹) initially, if total money with Ketan was ₹25200?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When final amounts are equal, the ratio of their principals is inversely proportional to their compound multiplying factors.

Time for Mahesh = 7 years, Time for David = 6 years. Difference = 1 year.

Ratio of Mahesh's share to David's share = 1 : (1 + 10/100)¹ = 10 : 11.

Total parts = 10 + 11 = 21 parts → ₹25200

David's share = (11 ÷ 21) × 25200 = 11 × 1200 = ₹13200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total wealth with Ketan = ₹25200

Age of Mahesh = 15 years

Age of David = 16 years

Target age for receiving money = 22 years

Rate of compound interest = 10% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Amount in Compound Interest: A = P(1 + R/100)T

Where P = Principal, R = Rate of interest, T = Time period
